Flight to Banjul

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When accountability takes off and taxpayers are left grounded

Unique Selling Point:
A government official insists on having his Dr title printed on an air ticket, costing the taxpayer millions of Rand.

Summary:
A pompous official fixated on title, is given a second chance at the public purse only to prove his so-called detractors right.

Further information:
In 2016, an elephant collided with a BMW X5 on the Mica-Hoedespruit Road in Limpopo.

The hungry elephant which had left the reserve in search of food, may have been on the right track after all.

The totalled BMW X5 belonged to none other than Mr Timothy Maake and may very well have been purchased with ill gotten gains.

Only a few months earlier, Maake had been fired from his position as the Municipal Manager of Mopani District Municipality on charges of gross misconduct. Allegedly, Maake enjoyed double dipping at the struggling municipality - earning a salary as a municipal manager while scoring tenders for his numerous companies through his employer.

After his dismissal, Maake seemingly dedicated himself to his businesses while building an academic record - of note, at least in his mind. In November 2024, like a phoenix, he rose from the ashes as the Secretary of the Limpopo Legislature. And no longer was he a mere “Mr” - NO - he was now Dr Timothy Maake.

But Maake’s ascent to the Secretary of the Limpopo Legislature came as a shock to opposition parties in council because they allegedly had no clue there was a key recruitment process in the works - spearheaded by the Speaker. They allege:-

No committee was formed to recruit Maake
He was deliberately shortlisted by junior staff members
HR & legal were not involved in the process and therefore, he was not vetted.
As a result, Maake wasn't even paid his first month's salary an no employment contract with government was in place

It's no wonder then, that Maake didn't take long to default to factory settings. Only a year in the prestigious position of Legislature Secretary and Maake is once again taking taxpayers for a ride. This time on a most bizarre tale of tickets to Banjul, Gambia.

The reason for the trip seemed simple enough: to attend the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association.
The process became a drama directed by none other than Maake who, like his allegedly questionable role as Limpopo’s Legislature Secretary wasn't even supposed to be a part of the delegation in the first place.

As the fifth wheel, Maake repeatedly insisted his academic “Dr” title appear on the ticket. Petty to no end, this resulted in unnecessary repeat cancellations of the group's tickets which ultimately cost taxpayers R 1.8 million.

Questions remain:-

Was due process followed in Maake’s appointment?
How was his murky past overridden?
Will Maake be rightfully forced to reimburse taxpayers for his childish ego trip?

Flight to Banjul
(Govan) Monday, November 17th 2025. We’re at the Limpopo Legislature following up on an
interview request.
(Govan) Things take an unexpected turn.
(Govan) Anyway, my name is Govan - I’m coming to follow up on…
(Kgatle Mashape) I said go out, go outside.
(Cameraman): Don't break my camera dude!
(Adv Franco Marx - DA) Police come help here this man is assaulting us!
(Govan) In a bizarre case of wasteful expenditure, this is the story of how a flight from South
Africa to The Gambian capital, Banjul became one of the most expensive business class
seats ever purchased for a government official. All to appease one man: career public
servant, Timothy Maake… Doctor Timothy Maake.
(Govan) It was on a road like this one nearly ten years ago, that a BMW X5 collided with an
elephant. Driving the vehicle was none other than Timothy Maake, the main character in this
story.
(Govan) Mopani District Municipality is in northeastern Limpopo, and includes a slice of the
Kruger Park.
(Govan) Between 2005 and 2016 Doctor Timothy Maake served as Mopani’s municipal
manager - basically, its CEO.
(Govan) According to opposition parties, it was a controversial time in office.
(Jacques Smalle) Gross misconduct, gross dereliction of duties, gross dishonesty…
(Govan) Three of eighteen charges brought by the Municipality against Maake. Jacques
Smalle is from the DA.
(Jacques Smalle)…..R 143 million of fruitless and wasteful expenditure, R 1 billion of
unauthorized expenditure and a debt that was just exceeding R 1 billion.
(Govan) In February 2016, the municipality accused Maake of playing fast and loose with the
municipal budget and dismissed him. He challenged it and eventually resigned under a cloud
in 2017.
(Govan) Conty Lebepe is a local activist.
(Conty Lebepe) Our people are still struggling. They go for maybe 3 kilos going to fetch the

water. Others, the lucky ones, they've got their own boreholes, but other people are buying
the water.
(Govan) Conty says this dysfunctional water pump station is an example of Maake’s legacy.
(Conty Lebepe) It's a disastrous legacy ---
(Conty Lebepe) When you speak about delivery, speak about something else, especially
when you speak about Maake, Mr. Maake, because I don't think he knows what the delivery
means, especially service delivery to the people.
(Govan) In short, Maake’s record is hardly stellar.
(Govan) In the same year he resigned, Timothy Maake completed a PhD in Public
Administration - his dissertation was titled Integrated development planning: A Case Study of
Mopani District Municipality.
(Govan) For the next decade, Maake reinvented himself as a businessman and governance
expert
(SABC News) For more on governance on the local and national level we’re joined by
governance expert, Dr Tim Maake. Very good evening Dr Maake, thank you for your time.
(Tim Maake) Thanks Mpho, good evening to you and good evening to the viewers.
(Govan) But that’s not where his re-emergence ended. This is the Limpopo Legislature,
where laws are passed and the provincial government is meant to be held accountable. It’s
here that Maake re-claimed a place in the public service last year.
(Govan) Doctor Timothy Maake is now Secretary of the Limpopo Legislature.
(Govan) Once again, he's like the body's CEO - but this time, he heads a much bigger and
more powerful organisation.
(Govan) This insider is familiar with the legislature’s workings.
(Insider) Someone like that should’ve never stepped foot in the legislature but you can always
understand it from the perspective where you’re looking at the person who hired him.
(Govan) He accuses the Speaker of the Limpopo Legislature, Doctor Makoma Makhurupetje,
of protecting Dr Maake and overlooking his checkered past.
(Insider) They are coming from the same region in Mopani.
(Makoma Makhurupetje) You may be seated

(Govan) With his authority cemented, it appears Doctor Maake picked up where he left off.
(Govan) How is he walking around?
(Insider) That guy’s strutting like a peacock.
(Govan) The allegations against him include flouting treasury’s guidelines by purchasing two
luxury vehicles for R 6 million for Dr Makhurupetje, as well as dishing out a favourable tender to
a family member and the unfair suspension of key executive managers.
(Govan) And that’s where The Gambia and its capital, Banjul, re-emerge in this story. Last
August, the city was host to the 54th Commonwealth Parliamentary Association - ironically, a
body established to support good governance.
(Insider) The Commonwealth Parliamentary Association is a body where most of the legislative
institutions come together to learn the best practices of how to run institutions in the era that
we’re in.
(Govan) The Limpopo legislature planned to send a seven person delegation - including its
secretary. The delegation’s tickets were booked in a batch for an initial cost of R1.3 million. But
then followed a bizarre drama, sparked by Maake himself.
(Insider) He saw in the tickets the Doctor title is not appearing
(Govan) So, it was Mr Tim Maake
(Insider) It was Mr Tim Maake
(Govan) Nothing wrong with that
(Govan) But apparently Maake disagrees.
(Insider) You need to tell the agent who booked this flight to change that title to Doctor title
(Govan) Dr Maake approved the cancellation of the flights?
(Govan) Because of an insistence of a Dr title?
(Insider) Absolutely.
(Govan) The adjustment affected the whole group, and came with a steep fee. Not only that:
it forced the delegation to change its route, adding three stops to the journey. And Maake’s

request was never granted. By the time he accepted that he’d have to travel as Mister, the
cost of the trip had ballooned by over R400 000.
(Conty Lebepe) He cancelled the flights only because his Doctor title - academic Doctor - was
not appearing on the flight ticket
(Govan) It's ridiculous,
(Conty) Very ridiculous.
(Govan) What did you think when you saw that?
(Conty) No, I just laughed and said no, we have been taken for granted as the taxpayers.
(Govan) Are you going to make sure he pays back that money himself?
(Jacques Smalle) The investigation must happen, so that a disciplinary process can be
instituted.
(Govan) Given that our interview with the DA is at the legislature, we decide to check if the
Doctor is in
(Govan) We have requested an interview with Dr Tim Maake: he’s not responded. His office
is just down there. I’m going to check if he’s there or at the very least if I can find out if he’ll
do the interview.
(Govan) I’m just coming to follow up on a request that we sent for an interview ma’am.
(Govan) We’re told to wait for the office manager.
(Kgatle Condry Mashape ) Then, why are you taking pictures?
(Govan) They’re taking pictures of me which they’re allowed to do, I guess
(Govan) Instead a man claiming to be the head of security arrives, and makes it very clear
neither we nor our cameras are welcome.
(Govan) Anyway, my name is Govan - Im coming to follow up on…
(Kgatle Condry Mashape) I said go out, go outside!
(Govan) Things quickly escalate.
(Cameraman) Are you trying to break my camera, dude?
(Govan) Hey, hey, hey… Don't touch his camera.

(Kgatle Condryy Mashape ) Go outside with your cameras.
(Govan) Don’t touch his cameras
(Govan) We’re forced downstairs and our producer begins recording as our cameramen are
under threat.
(Producer) Anything that’s going to happen, we’re going to get it on camera - OK, touch us!
(Govan) The man repeatedly refuses to identify himself…
(Govan) Who are you sir, what’s your name?
[Adv Franco Marx) Who are you?
(Kgatle Mashape) I’m coming to clean you.
(Adv Franco Marx - DA) I hope you record this!
(Producer) Please don’t touch me!
(Govan) Then, in full view of four police officers…He physically accosts our producer,
bending her fingers backwards.
(Govan) What are you doing?
(Advocate Franco Marx -DA) Police come help here! This guy is assaulting us!
(Govan) The police only intervene to ask us to leave.
(Police Officer) What are you guys doing here?
(Govan) We are journalists.
(Police Officer) With due respect: everyone go out now!
(Govan) He’s assaulted our producer and injured her finger. Who is he?
(Advocate Franco Marx - DA) Well I still don’t know, I know what you know - allegedly, he’s the
security manager here.
(Govan) We later learn that Kgatle Condry Mashape is a recent Maake appointee.
(Govan) He’s assaulted our producer who’s now injured and we don’t know what to do about it,

the police saw it happen and did nothing about it.
(Govan) Dr Maake declined an interview and denies all allegations. He says he wasn’t
dismissed and didn’t run the Mopani District Municipality into the ground. Dr Maake says before
his appointment, employees of the legislature never reported for work or did their jobs - but now
they do. He insists that he and Makhurupetje are both accountable to the legislature.
(Govan) Maake refuses to comment on the matter of Makhurupetje’s luxury vehicles, saying that
it, like all other matters involving Makurupetje, is before a Committee in the Legislature.
Regarding the flight to Banjul - he says there was no charge for cancelled tickets BUT our
information tells a different story.

In November 2024, like a phoenix, he rose from the ashes as the Secretary of the Limpopo Legislature. And no longer was he a mere “Mr” - NO - he was now Dr Timothy Maake. But Maake’s ascent to the Secretary of the Limpopo Legislature came as a shock to opposition parties in council because they allegedly had no clue there was a key recruitment process in the works - spearheaded by the Speaker. They allege:- No committee was formed to recruit Maake He was deliberately shortlisted by junior staff members HR & legal were not involved in the process and therefore, he was not vetted. As a result, Maake wasn't even paid his first month's salary an no employment contract with government was in place It's no wonder then, that Maake didn't take long to default to factory settings. Only a year in the prestigious position of Legislature Secretary and Maake is once again taking taxpayers for a ride. This time on a most bizarre tale of tickets to Banjul, Gambia. The reason for the trip seemed simple enough: to attend the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association. The process became a drama directed by none other than Maake who, like his allegedly questionable role as Limpopo’s Legislature Secretary wasn't even supposed to be a part of the delegation in the first place. As the fifth wheel, Maake repeatedly insisted his academic “Dr” title appear on the ticket. Petty to no end, this resulted in unnecessary repeat cancellations of the group's tickets which ultimately cost taxpayers R 1.8 million. Questions remain:- Was due process followed in Maake’s appointment? How was his murky past overridden? Will Maake be rightfully forced to reimburse taxpayers for his childish ego trip?
